pr.title: Call the product ArzoieMail in the developer docs; make README and ROADMAP agree
pr.body:
The developer docs called the product hMailServer. This PR changes the prose to ArzoieMail.

**Changed:** AGENTS.md, the `.claude/skills` (regression-first and the five upgrade-* skills), BUILDING.md, README.md, ROADMAP.md, `Tools/Administrator/README.md`, the SPF conformance README and `libraries/README.md`.

**Kept as hMailServer on purpose.** Existing installations, scripts and the web admin depend on these names, or the installer needs them to upgrade an hMailServer installation in place:
- the `hmailserver/` folder and the project files (`hMailServer.sln`, `.vcxproj`, `.idl`, `hMailServer Tools.sln`, `hMailServer Tests.sln`, `hMailServer64.iss`);
- `%hMailServerLibs%`;
- `hMailServer.exe`, `.ini` and `hMailAdmin.exe`;
- the service name and `NT SERVICE\hMailServer`;
- the `hMailServer.Application` COM API;
- the registry keys, the installer AppId, the `X-hMailServer-*` headers, the `hm_` tables and `hMailServerBackup.xml`.

AGENTS.md now lists these names with the reason, so nobody renames them by accident, and ROADMAP.md points to that list. References to upstream hMailServer (the 5.7.2 base, its forum, Martin Knafve) are unchanged.

**Not in this PR:** the end-user documentation book (`hmailserver/documentation/`, about 180 pages). It's a larger, separate piece of work: it is full of ini keys, COM names and paths that must keep their names, and it is published as a manual.

No code changes.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

### Second commit: README and ROADMAP now agree

Corrections to both files:
- **Upstream:** ROADMAP said upstream hMailServer is no longer maintained, which is wrong. ArzoieMail is based on hMailServer's code after 5.7.2, up to upstream `master` of 2026-10-11, and both files now say so.
- **Test count:** the README said 1,294 tests, a Phase 0 number. Master runs 1,313 tests and 1,204 pass. ROADMAP's baseline is now exact.
- **Security:** the README's security section and its "why things were replaced" table now cover the Phase 1 work: AES-GCM secrets under DPAPI with an exportable key, encrypted backups, the Administrator's DPAPI, and the logon timing fix. The Phase 1 row lists everything that phase did.
- **Phase 5:** it was "Ongoing" in the README but "planned" in ROADMAP. It is ongoing, and ROADMAP now describes the portable core (gcc/clang) and the SPF fuzzers we inherited, and what comes next.
- **Phase 6:** ROADMAP listed "new web admin" under Phase 6, but the web admin is Phase 1b.
- **Wording:** "installers", not "releases", are tested in VMs. The phase-order sentence now notes that code quality runs alongside the other phases.

+ArzoieMail is a free, open-source email server for Microsoft Windows, licensed under AGPLv3. It carries on hMailServer 5.7.2 as a project of its own. It implements SMTP, IMAP, and POP3, and runs as a Windows service. The codebase is written primarily in C++ (server core) and C# (admin tools), targeting C++20 with the Visual Studio 2026 v145 toolset, with 64-bit Windows builds.
+
+**Names that stay hMailServer.** The product is ArzoieMail in everything users read. Some identifiers keep the
+hMailServer name on purpose, because existing installations, scripts and the web admin depend on them, or so that

+- Passwords are hashed with Argon2id, and older hashes are upgraded when users log on. A logon

commit.message:
Call the product ArzoieMail in the developer docs

AGENTS.md, the skills, BUILDING.md and the READMEs under source and
libraries still called the product hMailServer. The prose now says
ArzoieMail. Identifiers keep their names: the source folder, project
files, hMailServer.exe and .ini, the service name, the
hMailServer.Application COM API, %hMailServerLibs% and the rest, so
the docs still match the code. References to upstream hMailServer, its
forum and its author stay as they are.

AGENTS.md now lists the names that stay hMailServer and why, and
ROADMAP.md points to that list. README no longer marks key export as
planned.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Make README and ROADMAP agree, and correct both

- ROADMAP said upstream hMailServer is no longer maintained; it is.
  The fork's base is hMailServer after 5.7.2, up to upstream master of
  2026-10-11, which both files now say.
- The README's test count (1,294) was from Phase 0; master runs 1,313
  tests, 1,204 of them pass. ROADMAP's baseline is now exact.
- The README's security section and its "why things were replaced"
  table did not mention the Phase 1 secrets work, encrypted backups,
  the Administrator's DPAPI or the logon timing fix; its Phase 1 row
  left out key export, the Argon2id review and UTF-8 credentials.
- Phase 6 in ROADMAP still listed a new web admin, which is Phase 1b.
- Phase 5 was "Ongoing" in README and "planned" in ROADMAP. It is
  ongoing, and ROADMAP now says what exists from upstream: the portable
  core built with gcc and clang, and the SPF fuzzers.
- The README now says installers, not releases, are tested in VMs, and
  that the phases run in order with code quality alongside.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

issue.title: Add notes for agents picking up the work (docs/agents)

repository.name: ArzoieMail
repository.description: ArzoieMail is a free, open-source email server for Windows, forked from hMailServer. It supports SMTP, IMAP and POP3, plus anti-spam, anti-virus, DKIM, SSL/TLS, backups, scripting and a COM API. Named after my daughter Arzoie and maintained in Delhi, India.

issue.body:
Adds `docs/agents/`, notes for the AI agents and people who pick up ArzoieMail work. They cover what ROADMAP.md, AGENTS.md and BUILDING.md don't, and link to those instead of copying them.

```
docs/agents/
  README.md              reading order, and how to keep these notes useful
  working-agreement.md   PRs and branch names, merging, phases, tests, reporting, security
  environment.md         dev machine, building tools/tests against the branch's type library,
                         CI checks (which are required), GitHub without gh, the Hyper-V VM
  gotchas.md             editing CRLF/BOM files, shell quoting, SQL scripts split at blank lines,
                         ISupportErrorInfo, tests waiting for delivery, flaky tests, CI, git
  handoffs/2026-10-26.md where Phase 1 left off, what waits on the maintainer, a Phase 1b brief
  tools/gh.py            the GitHub REST helper (token from Git Credential Manager; nothing stored)
```

Also in this PR:
- AGENTS.md points agents to `docs/agents/README.md`.
- The `handoff` skill now writes its note to `docs/agents/handoffs/YYYY-MM-DD.md` instead of the OS temp folder, so the next agent finds it. Lasting rules go in the topical files, not in the handoff.

While writing this I checked the `protect-master` ruleset. It requires the release build, `Tests / Regression tests`, `gcc` and `clang`, but the maintainer's account can bypass it. That's why #27 and #28 merged while their checks were still running. The notes now say to check first.

No credentials, tokens or personal data are in these files. The test VM's credentials stay outside the repository.
